messages.author: 6597c45f2a31b5d0
messages.subject: Re: dataprocess error SWATH data
parts:
Hi Taylor,

I took a look and it looks like you have duplicate rows in your dataset.   Taking an example of protein ID A0A4X2JR93 with peptide ID ISVYYNEATGGK, precursor charge 2, and fragment ion b3, you will see in your dataset that you have the same run reporting an intensity value for that fragment ion multiple times.  

```
library(tidyverse)
ms %>% filter(ProteinName == "A0A4X2JR93", PeptideSequence == "ISVYYNEATGGK", PrecursorCharge == 2, FragmentIon == "b3") %>% arrange(Run)
```

    ProteinName PeptideSequence PrecursorCharge FragmentIon ProductCharge IsotopeLabelType Condition BioReplicate   Run Intensity
         <char>          <char>           <int>      <char>         <int>           <char>    <char>       <char> <int>     <num>
 1:  A0A4X2JR93    ISVYYNEATGGK               2          b3             1                L  ACROSOME   ACROSOME_1     1 19442.901
 2:  A0A4X2JR93    ISVYYNEATGGK               2          b3             1                L  ACROSOME   ACROSOME_1     1  7469.349
 3:  A0A4X2JR93    ISVYYNEATGGK               2          b3             1                L  ACROSOME   ACROSOME_2     2 29086.096
 4:  A0A4X2JR93    ISVYYNEATGGK               2          b3             1                L  ACROSOME   ACROSOME_2     2  6994.622

From my understanding of SWATH, there should not be multiple measurements of the same fragment ion in the same run.  Did you by any chance use one of the MSstats converters to convert your data to MSstats format?  Also, which upstream spectral processing tool did you use for ID / quant?

By the way, you can run this command to find all of the duplicate rows:

```
library(tidyverse)
ms %>% group_by(ProteinName, PeptideSequence, PrecursorCharge, FragmentIon, ProductCharge, Run) %>% count() %>% filter(n >= 2)
```

Thanks,
Tony

messages.author: f1a226279cd36312
messages.subject: Re: dataprocess error SWATH data
parts:
Hi Tony,
Thanks so much for narrowing the issue down! The workflow for this data was:
  • Generation of an in silico spectral ion library using DIA-NN
  • Identification/quant of proteins using the SWATH app in Peakview
  • Conversion of Peakview output files (ion table and FDR table) to MSstats input file using this package https://github.com/bschulzlab/reformatMS
  • MSstats = dataProcess, groupComparison
This is the workflow used by the core facility I've been working with, and does not show the issue I reported above (dataprocess runs without error, allowing progression on to group comparison). In the end, I figured out this was most likely due to the msstats version they are using (v2.4), while I'm using v4.14. I needed to rerun the code because in addition to the group comparison, I wanted to:
  • include proteins found only in one condition
  • extract quantification values using the msstats quantification() function
I tried running the code on the core computer and from memory this older mststats version would not report proteins only in one condition, and the quantification() function was not supported/available.

My PhD student working on a different project using the same workflow has come up with a workaround, instead using:
  •  DIA-NN to generate both the in silico ion library and perform the ID and quant
  • Conversion of DIA-NN output file to MSstats input file using this package https://github.com/MiguelCos/MSstats_labelfree_preprocessing
  • MSstats = dataProcess, groupComparison, quantification
If you think the issue I encountered with the original workflow is in the conversion step, can you let me know of any other options for converting Peakview output > MSstats input? If there are no good options, I'll also reprocess this data through DIA-NN. 

Thanks again for your input, it's so helpful!

Cheers,
Taylor

Hi,

For DIANN, our group has a standardized converter in the MSstatsConvert package called DIANNtoMSstatsFormat.  I would recommend using that function for converting DIANN output to MSstats format.

For Peakview, we don't have a dedicated converter from peakview to MSstats format yet, but if you have some sample data, we can look into adding a new converter from Peakview output to MSstats format.  

Thanks,
Tony
